report_title: Remembering to Be Fair Again: Reproducing Non-Markovian Fairness in Sequential Decision Making
authors: Domonkos Nagy; Lohithsai Yadala Chanchu; Krystof Bobek; Xin Zhou; Jacobus Smit
cert_field: Event Certifications: reproml.org/MLRC/2025/Journal_Track; PLUS Certifications: Reproducibility Certification
original_title: FairQCM: non-Markovian fairness via memory augmentations and counterfactual reasoning
verdict_prose: confirm FairQCM outperforms standard baselines in fairness enforcement and sample efficiency; BUT alternative fairness metrics (Egalitarian, Gini) yield mixed results, counterfactual memories show limited impact and in extensions hurt performance especially in complex dynamic settings
per_claim: core superiority=CONFIRMED; counterfactual-memory benefit=REFUTED (hurts performance in extensions); alt-metric claims=MIXED

report_title: A Reproducibility Study of Decoupling Feature Extraction and Classification Layers for Calibrated Neural Networks
authors: Johanna D'Ciofalo Khodaverdian; Eric Banzuzi; Katharina Deckenbach
original_title: Two-Stage Training (TST) decoupling feature extraction and classification for calibrated NNs
verdict_prose: reproduce main results: most replicate with slight deviation for CIFAR100; extensions validate the claims and show transferability to different architectures

report_title: [Re] Explaining Temporal Graph Models through an Explorer-Navigator Framework
authors: Miklós Hamar; Matey Krastev; Kristiyan Danielov Hristov; David Beglou
original_title: Explaining Temporal Graph Models Through an Explorer-Navigator Framework (T-GNNExplainer)
verdict_prose: confirm that their explainer outperforms the other baselines across nearly all datasets and metrics; navigator helps bias search; can find exact influential event set
per_claim: superiority=CONFIRMED (nearly all datasets/metrics); NOTE second independent reproduction of same original as 9M2XqvH2SB (which is more critical)

report_title: Reproducibility Study of "Explaining RL Decisions with Trajectories"
authors: Clio Feng; Colin Bot; Bart den Boef; Bart Aaldering
verdict_prose: results affirm the effectiveness of the method both in reproduction and additional experiments; HOWEVER human study suggests explanations are more challenging to interpret for humans in more complex environments
per_claim: method effectiveness=CONFIRMED; human-interpretability in complex envs=WEAKENED; NOTE second reproduction of same original as QdeBbK5CSh

report_title: [Re] On the Reproducibility of Post-Hoc Concept Bottleneck Models
authors: Nesta Midavaine; Gregory Hok Tjoan Go; Diego Canez; Ioana Simion; Satchit Chatterji
verdict_prose: most of the authors' claims and results hold; claims on performance preservation and non-requirement of labeled concept datasets generally reproduced; the claim on model editing capabilities was NOT reproduced
per_claim: performance preservation=REPRODUCED; no-labeled-concepts-needed=REPRODUCED; model editing=NOT REPRODUCED

report_title: Reproducibility Study of "Learning Perturbations to Explain Time Series Predictions"
authors: Jiapeng Fan; Luke Cadigan; Paulius Skaisgiris; Sebastian Uriel Arias
cert_field: Event Certifications: reproml.org/MLRC/2023/Journal_Track; PLUS Certifications: Reproducibility Certification
original_title: Learning Perturbations to Explain Time Series Predictions (ExtremalMask)
verdict_prose: although discrepancies exist, results generally support the core of the original paper's conclusions; no OOD-sample flaw found on tested synthetic dataset
per_claim: (1) outperforms other models=SUPPORTED with discrepancies; (2) preservation>deletion game=SUPPORTED; OOD flaw=ABSENT on tested data

authors: Gijs de Jong; Macha J. Meijer; Derck W. E. Prinzhorn; Harold Ruiter
original_title: Fair Attribute Completion on Graph with Missing Attributes (FairAC)
verdict_prose: results of the original paper are reproducible and the claims hold; however the claim that FairAC is a generic framework for many downstream tasks is very broad and could only be partially tested
per_claim: core claims=REPRODUCED; genericity claim=ONLY PARTIALLY TESTABLE

report_title: Transfer Learning with Informative Priors: Simple Baselines Better than Previously Reported
authors: Ethan Harvey; Mikhail Petrov; Michael C Hughes
cert_field: Event Certifications: reproml.org/MLRC/2023/Journal_Track; PLUS Certifications: Reproducibility Certification
original_title: NOT_NAMED_IN_ABSTRACT (target = source-task-informed prior line of work; abstract says only 'Recent work suggests...')
verdict_prose: standard transfer learning (initialization only) performs far better than reported in previous comparisons; informative-prior gains vary: negative/negligible on 2 datasets, modest 1.5-3pts on 2, substantial >8pts on 1; mechanistic justification (loss-landscape alignment) not consistently supported
per_claim: prior-gains claims=WEAKENED (dataset-dependent, baseline underestimated); mechanism story=NOT SUPPORTED consistently

report_title: 'Explaining RL Decisions with Trajectories': A Reproducibility Study
authors: Karim Ahmed Abdel Sadek; Matteo Nulli; Joan Velja; Jort Vincenti
cert_field: Event Certifications: reproml.org/MLRC/2023/Journal_Track; PLUS Certifications: Reproducibility Certification
verdict_prose: claims (i) (ii) (iii) partially hold; claim (iv) humans correctly identify attributed trajectories COULD NOT be supported given limited extent of original experiments
per_claim: (i)=PARTIAL; (ii)=PARTIAL; (iii)=PARTIAL; (iv)=NOT SUPPORTED; NOTE second reproduction of same original as JQoWmeNaC2 (more positive)

authors: Markus Semmler; Miguel de Benito Delgado
cert_field: Event Certifications: reproml.org/MLRC/2023/Journal_Track; PLUS Certifications: Reproducibility Certification
original_title: CS-Shapley: Classwise-Shapley values for data valuation
verdict_prose: CS-Shapley helps in the scenarios it was originally tested in, in particular detection of corrupted labels; but it is outperformed by the conceptually simpler Data Banzhaf in detecting highly influential points
per_claim: original scenarios=REPRODUCED; dominance over simpler methods=REFUTED (Data Banzhaf wins)

report_title: Reproducibility Study of "ITI-GEN: Inclusive Text-to-Image Generation"
authors: Daniel Gallo Fernández; Răzvan-Andrei Matișan; Alejandro Monroy Muñoz; Janusz Partyka
verdict_prose: most claims hold: improves diversity and quality, scalable, plug-and-play, computationally efficient; HOWEVER sometimes uses undesired attributes as proxy features, cannot disentangle correlated attribute pairs (gender/baldness), training time grows exponentially with attribute count
per_claim: diversity/quality/scalability/plug-and-play/efficiency=HOLD; disentanglement=REFUTED for some pairs; scalability of training time=WEAKENED

report_title: Reproducibility study of "Robust Fair Clustering: A Novel Fairness Attack and Defense Framework"
authors: Lucas Ponticelli; Vincent Loos; Eren Kocadag; Kacper Bartosik
cert_field: Event Certifications: reproml.org/MLRC/2023/Journal_Track; PLUS Certifications: Reproducibility Certification
original_title: Robust Fair Clustering: A Novel Fairness Attack and Defense Framework (CFC defence)
verdict_prose: findings confirm the original paper's claims, reinforcing vulnerability of fair clustering models to adversarial attacks and robustness of the CFC mechanism; (Changes field documents two bugs found in original code, incl. missing random seeds for CFC)

report_title: [Re] CUDA: Curriculum of Data Augmentation for Long-tailed Recognition
original_title: CUDA: Curriculum of Data Augmentation for Long-Tailed Recognition
verdict_prose: successfully replicated all of the results pertaining to the long-tailed CIFAR-100-LT dataset (scope limited to that dataset); extended analysis of how CUDA tackles class imbalance
per_claim: CIFAR-100-LT results=ALL REPLICATED; other datasets=NOT TESTED in reproduction

report_title: [Re] Reproducibility Study of "Explaining Temporal Graph Models Through an Explorer-Navigator Framework"
authors: Helia Ghasemi; Christina Isaicu; Jesse Wonnink; Andreas Berentzen
original_title: Explaining Temporal Graph Models Through an Explorer-Navigator Framework (T-GNNExplainer)
verdict_prose: main lines hold up even though all results are less pronounced than claimed; performs best on some but NOT all metrics; does not perform similarly across different T-GNN models; simpler cheaper explainers (PBONE) competitive
per_claim: superiority=WEAKENED (not all metrics, less pronounced); NOTE second reproduction of same original as FI1XvwpchC (which was more positive) - witness disagreement
